125	**Summary:** Added the interactive and uiform foundation packages (tasks 4.5 and 4.7), completing Section 4 of the add-harnaas-foundation change and taking it from 26/74 to 28/74 tasks with fmt, lint and tests all clean.

127	**Changes:**
128	- cmd/harnaas/cli/interactive resolves whether harnaas may prompt from the command's own streams plus the environment — HARNAAS_TEST_TTY override, then go test, then coding-agent sentinels (CLAUDECODE, CURSOR_AGENT, GEMINI_CLI, COPILOT_CLI, PI_CODING_AGENT), then CI, then both streams being terminals — with the decision biased towards 'no' because a flag-driven path always exists while a prompt shown to something that cannot answer hangs rather than degrades

135	- uiform.Confirm consults the context directly before and after running the form, because huh reports a cancelled context as ErrTimeout and ignores the context entirely in accessible mode
136	- Test coverage: a table over every prompting gate including piped streams and the CI=false escape hatch, each agent sentinel individually, real os.Pipe and bytes.Buffer both answering 'not a terminal', the styling gates, accessible mode completing a prompt against non-terminal streams, cancellation reported separately from declining, and the theme's unstyled-titles and accent-selection guarantees

144	- Accessible mode is what makes a prompt testable at all: the full-screen path needs a terminal to redraw, while runAccessible works against a strings.Reader and a bytes.Buffer. 160	- Two AST guardrails over non-test sources: the package imports no filesystem, network or environment package (encoding 'data only, no write behaviour'), and declares no package init so the roster stays a readable literal
161	- CLAUDE.md records the two load-bearing decisions — the roster is data only with the caller doing I/O, and an unrecognized id is an error because the harnesses list states a guarantee rather than exclusivity
162	- Tasks 5.1 through 5.4 checked off in openspec/changes/add-harnaas-foundation/tasks.md
163

165	- The reference entire.io CLI's agent registry is init()-registered into a mutex-guarded map, which harnaas cannot copy: package init is banned and a map gives a different iteration order every run, while the roster's order is what an 'unknown harness' message and a scaffolded manifest are both built from. 166	- The harness roster genuinely earns its own package under the 'extract only to break an import cycle' rule: add-harnaas-install's adapters will import it, and the flat cli package will import the adapters — so a roster living in the flat package would be a cycle one change later.

168	- ADR 0003 establishes CLAUDE.md as Claude Code-specific (AGENTS.md is the shared file it bridges from), which is what makes CLAUDE.md sound detection evidence where AGENTS.md would not be — AGENTS.md is read by several harnesses and would detect all of them or none.
169	- goconst fires at three occurrences of a string literal inside a single test function, so a scratch value used to prove a defensive copy has to be a local const.

172	
173	**Summary:** Added the manifest document, strict decoding and root-only discovery package (Section 6, tasks 6.1–6.8), taking the add-harnaas-foundation change from 32/74 to 40/74 tasks with fmt, lint and tests all clean.
174	
175	**Changes:**
176	- cmd/harnaas/cli/manifest declares the decoded document — integer version, harnesses, sources map and an assets array whose entries keep their array index and their written form — with every field uninterpreted: an empty field means 'not declared', never 'declared as the default', which is the distinction the interpretation layer needs to default targets and scope

180	- Every decode failure returns a nil document, so a partially decoded manifest can never reach a later phase and install a subset of what the project declared while reporting success
181	- manifest.Load resolves the manifest from the context-carried project root, and manifest.Path is the single place the file's location is assembled so init and install cannot disagree about where it is
182	- The search for a harnaas.json below the root runs before the missing-manifest check and skips dot-directories plus node_modules and vendor: a vendored library's manifest is its own, and a project whose only manifest sits in a subdirectory is never told to run `harnaas init`
183	- Three diagnostics: *DecodeError carrying location, a one-line problem and an edit; *NotFoundError naming `harnaas init`; and *SubdirectoryError naming the file that will never be read and the one harnaas does read
184	- Test coverage for section 6.8 plus a table asserting the problem-then-fix shape across all ten failure modes, that no remedy offers a fix command, and an AST guardrail over non-test sources asserting no write call and no jsonutil import has crept into the read-only loader
185	- CLAUDE.md records the two new load-bearing decisions — the version pre-pass and the root-only rule with its dependency-directory skips — and .golangci.yaml exempts paths.ProjectRoot from wrapcheck, because its error is already a finished user-facing diagnostic that a caller would only prefix with plumbing
186	
187	**Learnings:**
188	- json.Unmarshal validates the whole input and rejects a second top-level value, so a version pre-pass over the full document makes an explicit trailing-data check unreachable — the check was written, proved dead, and removed in favour of documenting that the pre-pass settles it.
189	- encoding/json reports an unknown field as a bare fmt.Errorf, not a typed error, so recognising it means matching the literal prefix `json: unknown field ` and unquoting the rest; the translation falls through to reporting the raw message if that wording ever changes, which is worse but never wrong.
190	- An asset entry decoded from its own json.RawMessage carries offsets relative to the entry, so any line:column derived from them names the wrong line in the file. Scoping the locator to an entry and having it refuse to report a location at all is the fix — one comment in one place rather than a mutation at each call site.
191	- wrapcheck fires on errors returned from any other package including same-module ones, which will hit every future command calling paths.ProjectRoot. Configuring extra-ignore-sigs once is the right answer where the callee's error is already a complete problem-then-fix diagnostic; wrapping it would prefix a finished message with the caller's plumbing.
192	- The `exhaustive` linter's default (default-signifies-exhaustive: false) makes a switch on reflect.Kind a lint failure even with a default clause, which is a practical reason to describe expected JSON shapes from a field-name table rather than by reflection — and the table produces better messages anyway.
193	- Section 7's interpretation layer is now fully unblocked: it reads Document/AssetEntry, and the two decode-time distinctions it depends on are already pinned by tests — nil vs empty Targets, and empty-string overrides meaning undeclared.

- WriteFileAtomic removes the staging file unconditionally via defer on both success and failure, and flushes the destination directory best-effort after the rename so a crash cannot leave new contents on disk behind a directory entry still pointing at the old file

This is the boundary that decides which dropped errors need a suppression and which do not.
- testifylint's encoded-compare rule rejects asserting an exact JSON string with assert.Equal and pushes toward assert.JSONEq, which would defeat a test whose whole subject is indentation and trailing newline. Splitting the document on newlines and comparing the resulting []string satisfies the linter and reads better, because a failure names the line that moved.

**Learnings:**
- huh v2 reports a cancelled context as huh.ErrTimeout, not ErrUserAborted or context.Canceled — its run() maps tea.ErrProgramKilled to ErrTimeout because a timeout is the only reason it cancels a context itself. Matching on huh's error alone silently misclassifies a signal-driven cancellation; consulting ctx.Err() is the only reliable test.
- huh's accessible path (runAccessible) ignores the context entirely and runs synchronously against the given reader/writer, so a cancellation arriving mid-question is invisible until the prompt returns. Any wrapper that must honour cancellation has to check the context after the run as well as before it.
- Accessible mode is what makes a prompt testable at all: the full-screen path needs a terminal to redraw, while runAccessible works against a strings.Reader and a bytes.Buffer. A test that sets ACCESSIBLE and completes a prompt on non-terminal streams is therefore a genuine assertion that accessible mode was honoured, not a proxy for one.
- huh's accessible PromptString breaks out of its re-prompt loop on EOF rather than looping forever, and an empty line falls through to the default — so a test can feed a bare reader without hanging.

- manifest.Load resolves the manifest from the context-carried project root, and manifest.Path is the single place the file's location is assembled so init and install cannot disagree about where it is

- Test coverage for section 6.8 plus a table asserting the problem-then-fix shape across all ten failure modes, that no remedy offers a fix command, and an AST guardrail over non-test sources asserting no write call and no jsonutil import has crept into the read-only loader
- CLAUDE.md records the two new load-bearing decisions — the version pre-pass and the root-only rule with its dependency-directory skips — and .golangci.yaml exempts paths.ProjectRoot from wrapcheck, because its error is already a finished user-facing diagnostic that a caller would only prefix with plumbing

**Learnings:**
- json.Unmarshal validates the whole input and rejects a second top-level value, so a version pre-pass over the full document makes an explicit trailing-data check unreachable — the check was written, proved dead, and removed in favour of documenting that the pre-pass settles it.
- encoding/json reports an unknown field as a bare fmt.Errorf, not a typed error, so recognising it means matching the literal prefix `json: unknown field ` and unquoting the rest; the translation falls through to reporting the raw message if that wording ever changes, which is worse but never wrong.
- An asset entry decoded from its own json.RawMessage carries offsets relative to the entry, so any line:column derived from them names the wrong line in the file. Scoping the locator to an entry and having it refuse to report a location at all is the fix — one comment in one place rather than a mutation at each call site.
- wrapcheck fires on errors returned from any other package including same-module ones, which will hit every future command calling paths.ProjectRoot. Configuring extra-ignore-sigs once is the right answer where the callee's error is already a complete problem-then-fix diagnostic; wrapping it would prefix a finished message with the caller's plumbing.
- The `exhaustive` linter's default (default-signifies-exhaustive: false) makes a switch on reflect.Kind a lint failure even with a default clause, which is a practical reason to describe expected JSON shapes from a field-name table rather than by reflection — and the table produces better messages anyway.
- Section 7's interpretation layer is now fully unblocked: it reads Document/AssetEntry, and the two decode-time distinctions it depends on are already pinned by tests — nil vs empty Targets, and empty-string overrides meaning undeclared.

244	- **THEN** validation fails naming that harness, and the asset is not silently installed at project
245	  scope
246

248	
249	- **WHEN** the manifest declares an `instruction` asset at `user` scope
250	- **THEN** validation fails naming the asset and pointing to `rule` as the type for that intent,

252

254	
255	- **WHEN** an asset of type `instruction` declares scope `user`
256	- **THEN** validation fails reporting that instructions are project scope only
257

259	
260	Validation SHALL run over the whole decoded document and report every violation it finds rather than
261	stopping at the first. An id, whether inferred or declared, MUST be unique among assets of the same
262	type and MUST be a single safe path segment containing no path separator and no parent-directory
263	segment. A document with any violation MUST NOT be used by any later phase.

271	
272	- **WHEN** a declared id contains a path separator or a parent-directory segment
273	- **THEN** validation fails reporting that an id must be a single safe path segment
274	
275	#### Scenario: All violations are reported together
276	
277	- **WHEN** a manifest contains several independent violations
278	- **THEN** the reported error describes every violation rather than stopping at the first
279

281	
282	The manifest SHALL declare an integer `version`; version `1` is defined by this specification. A
283	version greater than harnaas understands MUST be refused with a message saying the manifest was
284	written by a newer harnaas and telling the user to upgrade, rather than attempting a partial read. A
285	missing or non-integer `version` MUST be an error.
286	
287	#### Scenario: Known version loads
288	
289	- **WHEN** the manifest declares version `1`
290	- **THEN** it is decoded according to this specification
291	
292	#### Scenario: Newer version is refused with guidance
293	
294	- **WHEN** the manifest declares a version greater than harnaas understands
295	- **THEN** loading fails saying the manifest was written by a newer harnaas and telling the user to
296	  upgrade, and no asset is processed
297	
298	#### Scenario: Missing version is rejected
299	
300	- **WHEN** the manifest omits `version`
301	- **THEN** loading fails reporting that the version field is required

An asset entry given as a string SHALL take one of two forms: `<sourceKey>:<path>`, where the key is
declared in `sources` and the path is relative to that source's root; or a project-local path
beginning with `.harnaas/`. A string in neither form — an unprefixed relative path, an absolute path,
or a URL — MUST be rejected, naming the entry and both accepted forms.

#### Scenario: Keyed remote form is accepted

- **WHEN** an asset string is `acme:skills/review` and `acme` is declared in `sources`
- **THEN** it resolves to the path `skills/review` within that source

#### Scenario: Local form is accepted

- **WHEN** an asset string is `.harnaas/rules/house-style.md`
- **THEN** it resolves to that path beneath the project's `.harnaas` directory

#### Scenario: Unprefixed path is rejected

- **WHEN** an asset string is `skills/review` with no source key and no `.harnaas/` prefix
- **THEN** loading fails naming the entry and stating both accepted forms

### Requirement: Local Source Containment Under .harnaas

A local asset path SHALL be relative to the project root and SHALL resolve inside `.harnaas`. A path
that is absolute, or that escapes `.harnaas` by traversing upward with parent-directory segments,
MUST be rejected at load time reporting that local assets live under `.harnaas`, and its content MUST
NOT be read.

#### Scenario: Upward traversal is rejected

- **WHEN** a local asset path escapes `.harnaas` using parent-directory segments
- **THEN** loading fails reporting that local assets must live under `.harnaas`

#### Scenario: Absolute local path is rejected

- **WHEN** a local asset entry names an absolute filesystem path
- **THEN** loading fails reporting that local asset paths must be relative to the project root

### Requirement: Type And Id Inferred From The Asset Path

An asset's type and id SHALL be inferred from its path: the containing directory names the type —
`skills/` → skill, `rules/` → rule, `instructions/` → instruction, `commands/` → command, `agents/` →
persona — and the leaf names the id, with any file extension removed. A path whose containing
directory is none of those names MUST be rejected, naming the entry and directing the author to the
object form.

#### Scenario: Skill inferred from a keyed path

- **WHEN** an asset string is `acme:skills/review`
- **THEN** the asset has type `skill` and id `review`

#### Scenario: Persona inferred from an agents directory

- **WHEN** an asset string is `acme:agents/reviewer`
- **THEN** the asset has type `persona` and id `reviewer`

#### Scenario: Extension stripped from a local file asset

- **WHEN** an asset string is `.harnaas/instructions/tone.md`
- **THEN** the asset has type `instruction` and id `tone`

#### Scenario: Unrecognized containing directory is rejected

- **WHEN** an asset string is `acme:prompts/review`, whose containing directory names no type
- **THEN** loading fails naming the entry and stating that the object form must declare the type

### Requirement: Asset Object Override Form

An asset entry given as an object SHALL carry its source string plus any of `type`, `id`, `targets`
and `scope`, each overriding what the path would otherwise imply or the manifest would otherwise
default to. The object form SHALL be the only way to state a per-asset type, id, target list or
scope, and it MUST be decoded as strictly as the rest of the document.

#### Scenario: Object supplies type and id for an unconventional layout

- **WHEN** an asset object names a source path whose directory does not follow the convention and
  declares `type` and `id` explicitly
- **THEN** the declared type and id are used and no inference from the path is attempted

#### Scenario: Object narrows the target list

- **WHEN** an asset object declares `targets` while the manifest also declares `harnesses`
- **THEN** the asset's effective targets are those declared on the object

#### Scenario: Unknown field in an asset object is rejected

- **WHEN** an asset object carries a key outside the accepted set
- **THEN** loading fails naming the unknown field and the asset

### Requirement: Target Defaulting

An asset's effective target list SHALL be the `targets` declared on its object form when present, and
the manifest's `harnesses` list otherwise. An asset whose effective target list is empty MUST be
rejected, since it could never be installed anywhere. A target naming a harness harnaas does not
recognize MUST be rejected, naming it and listing the recognized ones.

#### Scenario: Targets inherit the top-level harness list

- **WHEN** the manifest lists harnesses `["claude-code"]` and an asset declares no targets
- **THEN** that asset's effective targets are `["claude-code"]`

#### Scenario: Empty effective target list is rejected

- **WHEN** an asset declares no targets and the manifest declares no harnesses
- **THEN** validation fails reporting that the asset has no target harness

#### Scenario: Unknown harness name is rejected

- **WHEN** the manifest targets a harness harnaas does not recognize
- **THEN** validation fails naming the unknown harness and listing the recognized ones

### Requirement: Scope Defaulting And User-Scope Validity

An asset's `scope` SHALL default to `project`. `user` scope SHALL be accepted only for a target
harness the harness roster records as having an unambiguous per-user location; declaring it for any
other target MUST be a validation error naming the harness, never a silent fall back to project
scope. An `instruction` asset SHALL be project scope only, and declaring `user` scope on one MUST be
rejected.

#### Scenario: Scope defaults to project

- **WHEN** an asset declares no scope
- **THEN** it installs beneath the project root of each of its target harnesses

#### Scenario: User scope accepted where the roster records a per-user location

- **WHEN** an asset declares scope `user` and targets a harness the roster records as having a
  per-user location
- **THEN** the asset is marked for that harness's per-user location

#### Scenario: User scope rejected where the roster records none

- **WHEN** an asset declares scope `user` for a target harness with no unambiguous per-user location
- **THEN** validation fails naming that harness, and the asset is not silently installed at project
  scope

#### Scenario: User-scoped instruction is refused

- **WHEN** the manifest declares an `instruction` asset at `user` scope
- **THEN** validation fails naming the asset and pointing to `rule` as the type for that intent,
  because at user scope there is no clone for the content to survive

#### Scenario: User scope on an instruction is rejected

- **WHEN** an asset of type `instruction` declares scope `user`
- **THEN** validation fails reporting that instructions are project scope only

### Requirement: Manifest Semantic Validation

Validation SHALL run over the whole decoded document and report every violation it finds rather than
stopping at the first. An id, whether inferred or declared, MUST be unique among assets of the same
type and MUST be a single safe path segment containing no path separator and no parent-directory
segment. A document with any violation MUST NOT be used by any later phase.

#### Scenario: Duplicate id within a type is rejected

- **WHEN** two assets of type `skill` resolve to the same id from different sources
- **THEN** validation fails naming the duplicated id and both entries

#### Scenario: Unsafe id is rejected

- **WHEN** a declared id contains a path separator or a parent-directory segment
- **THEN** validation fails reporting that an id must be a single safe path segment

#### Scenario: All violations are reported together

- **WHEN** a manifest contains several independent violations
- **THEN** the reported error describes every violation rather than stopping at the first

### Requirement: Manifest Version Handling

The manifest SHALL declare an integer `version`; version `1` is defined by this specification. A
version greater than harnaas understands MUST be refused with a message saying the manifest was
written by a newer harnaas and telling the user to upgrade, rather than attempting a partial read. A
missing or non-integer `version` MUST be an error.

#### Scenario: Known version loads

- **WHEN** the manifest declares version `1`
- **THEN** it is decoded according to this specification

#### Scenario: Newer version is refused with guidance

- **WHEN** the manifest declares a version greater than harnaas understands
- **THEN** loading fails saying the manifest was written by a newer harnaas and telling the user to
  upgrade, and no asset is processed

#### Scenario: Missing version is rejected

- **WHEN** the manifest omits `version`
- **THEN** loading fails reporting that the version field is required

1	// Package manifest decodes `harnaas.json`, the committed, hand-edited file in
2	// which a project declares which harness assets it wants and where they come
3	// from.
4	//
5	// The package covers the document and nothing beyond it: where the file lives,
6	// and how its bytes become a [Document]. It does not interpret an asset's
7	// source string, infer a type or an id from a path, default a target list or a
8	// scope, or check any of them against the harness roster. Those read a decoded
9	// document and live in the manifest's interpretation layer, which is why this
10	// package imports no roster and validates no meaning — a field it accepts here
11	// is one it could read, not one harnaas has agreed to.
12	//
13	// # Strict decoding
14	//
15	// The manifest is written by a person and reviewed by a team, so an unknown
16	// field is nearly always a typo and surfacing it immediately is worth the cost
17	// of refusing to run. That is the whole test: strictness follows who writes the
18	// file, not what the file is called. `harnaas.lock.json` is machine-written and
19	// therefore decodes leniently, because a newer binary introduces fields an
20	// older binary would otherwise reject, bricking the file for everyone still on
21	// the older version.
22	//
23	// The version field is what bounds that trade. It is read on its own, ahead of
24	// the strict pass, so a manifest written by a newer harnaas is refused with an
25	// explicit "upgrade harnaas" message rather than a confusing complaint about
26	// the first field this binary happens not to know.
27	//
28	// A decode failure returns no document at all. Half a manifest is not a smaller
29	// manifest — it is a different one, and installing from it would place a subset
30	// of what the project declared while reporting success.
31	//
32	// # Read-only
33	//
34	// Nothing here writes. Apart from `harnaas init` creating the file once, harnaas
35	// never writes, reformats or normalizes `harnaas.json`: it is the artifact a
36	// team reviews, and a tool that rewrites it makes its diffs untrustworthy. Every
37	// remedy this package reports is therefore phrased as the exact edit for a
38	// person to make, never as a command that would make it for them. A test over
39	// this package's own sources asserts no write call has crept in.
40	package manifest
41	
42	// FileName is the manifest's only accepted name, at the repository root.
43	//
44	// It is a constant rather than a flag because the file is a project-level
45	// declaration: a `--manifest` pointing somewhere else would mean two developers
46	// in the same repository could install different asset sets and both be right.
47	const FileName = "harnaas.json"
48	
49	// SupportedVersion is the manifest schema version this binary understands.
50	//
51	// A manifest declaring a greater version is refused with an upgrade message
52	// rather than read partially, because the fields this binary would silently
53	// ignore are exactly the ones the newer harnaas added to change what the
54	// document means.
55	const SupportedVersion = 1
56	
57	// Document is a decoded manifest, field for field as written.
58	//
59	// Nothing in it has been interpreted: `Harnesses` and each entry's `Targets`
60	// are the strings the author typed rather than roster ids, and an asset's
61	// `Type`, `ID` and `Scope` are populated only where the object form declared
62	// them. An empty field here means "not declared", never "declared as the
63	// default" — the interpretation layer is what turns the first into the second,
64	// and it can only do that if decoding kept them distinguishable.
65	type Document struct {
66		// Path is the file the document was decoded from, so a later diagnostic can
67		// name it. It is empty for a document decoded from bytes.
68		Path string
69	
70		// Version is the declared schema version, always a version this binary
71		// understands — a greater one fails decoding rather than reaching a caller.
72		Version int
73	
74		// Harnesses names the harnesses assets target by default. The list states a
75		// guarantee ("we guarantee the declared assets work for these"), not
76		// exclusivity: assets installed for one harness are routinely visible to
77		// another.
78		Harnesses []string
79	
80		// Sources maps a short key to a source string such as
81		// `github:acme/assets@v1.2.0`. The key is what asset entries reference, so a
82		// repository and a ref appear exactly once each.
83		Sources map[string]string
84	
85		// Assets is the declared asset list in document order. Order is preserved
86		// because it is the order the author reads in review, and every diagnostic
87		// naming an entry names its index in this slice.
88		Assets []AssetEntry
89	}
90	
91	// AssetEntry is one entry of the `assets` array, in whichever form it was
92	// written.
93	//
94	// The string form carries only a source; the object form may additionally
95	// declare a type, an id, a target list or a scope, each suppressing what would
96	// otherwise be inferred or defaulted for that one field.
97	type AssetEntry struct {
98		// Index is the entry's position in the `assets` array. It is not decoded
99		// from the document — it is where the entry was found, and it is how every
100		// diagnostic points the author at the line to edit, since an entry has no
101		// other stable name until its id is known.
102		Index int
103	
104		// ObjectForm records whether the entry was written as an object rather than
105		// a bare source string. Some remedies are only available in the object form,
106		// so a message can direct an author there only if it knows they are not
107		// already using it.
108		ObjectForm bool
109	
110		// Source is the entry's source string: the `<sourceKey>:<path>` or
111		// `.harnaas/…` form, exactly as written and not yet parsed.
112		Source string
113	
114		// Type overrides the type the path would imply. Empty means undeclared.
115		Type string
116	
117		// ID overrides the id the path's leaf would imply. Empty means undeclared.
118		ID string
119	
120		// Targets overrides the manifest's `harnesses` list for this asset. A nil
121		// slice means undeclared; an empty non-nil slice means the author declared
122		// an empty list, which is a validation error rather than a default, because
123		// the asset could never be installed anywhere.
124		Targets []string
125	
126		// Scope overrides the default `project` scope. Empty means undeclared.
127		Scope string
128	}
129

3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"path/filepath"
6	)

8	// DecodeError reports a manifest harnaas could not decode.
9	//
10	// One type covers every decoding failure — malformed JSON, an unknown field, a
11	// wrongly shaped field, a version this binary cannot read — because they all
12	// end in the same place: a person opening `harnaas.json` and editing one line.
13	// What differs between them is the sentence, not the shape, and the shape is
14	// what a caller would branch on.
15	type DecodeError struct {
16		// Path is the manifest the failure came from. It is empty for a document
17		// decoded from bytes, where the message falls back to naming the file.
18		Path string
19	
20		// Problem states what is wrong, in one line.
21		Problem string
22	
23		// Fix states the edit that resolves it. It is always an edit for a person to
24		// make: harnaas does not write this file.
25		Fix string
26	
27		// Line and Column locate the problem in the file, both 1-based, and are zero
28		// where the failure has no single location — an entry named by its index, or
29		// a version that is wrong wherever it was written.
30		Line, Column int
31	}
32	
33	// Error renders the location, the problem, a blank line, and the fix.
34	func (e *DecodeError) Error() string {
35		return fmt.Sprintf("%s: %s\n\n%s", e.where(), e.Problem, e.Fix)
36	}
37	
38	// where names the file and, where one is known, the line and column inside it,
39	// in the `file:line:column` form an editor and a terminal both make clickable.
40	func (e *DecodeError) where() string {
41		name := e.Path
42		if name == "" {
43			name = FileName
44		}
45		if e.Line <= 0 {
46			return name
47		}
48		return fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d:%d", name, e.Line, e.Column)
49	}
50	
51	// NotFoundError reports a project with no manifest at its root.
52	//
53	// It is a distinct type because "there is no manifest yet" is not a broken
54	// manifest: it is the ordinary state of a project before `harnaas init`, and a
55	// caller may want to say something different about it.
56	type NotFoundError struct {
57		// Root is the project root that was searched, so the message can show which
58		// project harnaas resolved — the usual cause of surprise here is being in a
59		// different repository than expected.
60		Root string
61	}
62	
63	// Error names the project searched and the command that creates the file.
64	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string {
65		return fmt.Sprintf(
66			"no %s found in %s\n\n"+
67				"Run `harnaas init` in that project to create one.",
68			FileName, e.Root,
69		)
70	}
71	
72	// SubdirectoryError reports a `harnaas.json` below the project root.
73	//
74	// Such a file is an error rather than something harnaas quietly skips. A file
75	// with this name that harnaas ignores is worse than one it rejects: its author
76	// believes it is declaring assets, and every command silently disagrees.
77	// Merging it is not on the table either, since the effective asset set would
78	// then depend on which directory a command ran from, which is exactly the
79	// variation harnaas exists to remove.
80	type SubdirectoryError struct {
81		// Path is the offending manifest's absolute path.
82		Path string
83	
84		// Root is the project root, whose manifest is the only one harnaas reads.
85		Root string
86	}
87	
88	// Error names the file that will never be read and states the only manifest
89	// harnaas does read.
90	func (e *SubdirectoryError) Error() string {
91		shown := e.Path
92		if relative, err := filepath.Rel(e.Root, e.Path); err == nil {
93			shown = filepath.ToSlash(relative)
94		}
95	
96		return fmt.Sprintf(
97			"found a second manifest at %s, which harnaas never reads\n\n"+
98				"harnaas reads only the %s at the repository root (%s). "+
99				"Move any entries you need into that file and delete %s.",
100			shown, FileName, e.Root, shown,
101		)
102	}

content.content:
This is why there is no `add`, `remove` or `update` command: they would exist only to edit a file a
person can edit.

The reason is that the manifest is the artifact a team reviews. A tool that rewrites it makes its diffs
untrustworthy — a reviewer can no longer tell an intentional pin bump from a normalization pass — and
reformatting churn would land in every pull request that ran a command. Phrasing every remedy as an
exact edit rather than a fix command also keeps the human in the loop on the one decision that
actually matters: which version of somebody else's content this repository is about to trust.

### An asset's type and id are inferred from its path, with an object form as the escape hatch

`acme:skills/review` says everything: the containing directory names the type, the leaf names the id.
Writing `{"source": "acme:skills/review", "type": "skill", "id": "review"}` would restate in twelve
tokens what the path already said, and would introduce a second source of truth that can disagree with
the first.

The convention is not invented here — `skills/`, `commands/` and `agents/` are already how asset
repositories are laid out, because that is how the harnesses themselves read them. Inference makes the
common case one string per asset, which keeps the manifest short enough to review as a list. A path
whose containing directory names no type is an error that points at the object form rather than a
guess, so the failure mode is a message rather than an asset silently installed as the wrong type.

The object form then carries the genuinely per-asset decisions that no path can express — a narrowed
`targets` list and a non-default `scope` — so there is exactly one place to look when an asset behaves
differently from its neighbours.

### Sources are declared once under a key, and assets reference the key

A repository and ref appear exactly once, in `sources`. The alternative — a full `github:acme/assets@v1.2.0`
prefix on every asset string — makes a version bump an N-line edit where N is the number of assets from
that repository, and makes it possible for two assets to disagree about which ref they came from while
both look correct in review.

Keying also gives the later changes a natural unit: `install` fetches one archive per repository and
commit regardless of how many assets it covers, and `lint` checks for a newer tag once per source
rather than once per asset. Both fall out of the manifest shape instead of needing a deduplication
pass.

### The `harnesses` list states a guarantee, not exclusivity

Because skills and instructions land in shared locations that many harnesses read — see
[0002-shared-agents-target-before-per-harness.md](../../../docs/adr/0002-shared-agents-target-before-per-harness.md)
— a harness that is *not* in the list will still see assets installed for one that is. The list
therefore means "the harnesses we guarantee this works for", not "the harnesses that can see this".

This matters to the manifest's validation rules, which is why it is settled here: an unrecognized
harness name is an error because it is a guarantee harnaas cannot make, but an asset installed for
`claude-code` being visible to Cursor is not a bug to be prevented. It also sets what `init`'s
detection is for — pre-filling a list of guarantees, not enumerating what is installed on the machine.

### Scope defaults to project, and `user` is validated rather than degraded

`user` scope is accepted only where a target harness has an unambiguous per-user location, and
declaring it elsewhere is a validation error. Silently falling back to project scope would install the
asset somewhere the author did not ask for and would not notice, and a wrong install location is
exactly the failure harnaas exists to eliminate.

An `instruction` is project scope only, and that is a definitional consequence rather than a
limitation: an instruction differs from a rule by surviving a fresh clone inside a committed file —
see
[0003-instruction-content-in-an-agents-md-block.md](../../../docs/adr/0003-instruction-content-in-an-agents-md-block.md).
At user scope there is no clone and no committed file, so the distinction from a rule disappears and
the type would mean nothing.

### One manifest, at the repository root

A `harnaas.json` in a subdirectory is an error naming the root manifest, not a second declaration to
be merged. Merging would make the effective asset set depend on which directory a command ran from,
which contradicts the whole point: the repository declares one set of assets and everyone gets it.
Erroring instead of ignoring is deliberate too — a file named `harnaas.json` that harnaas silently
skips is worse than one it rejects.

### A data-only harness roster ships before the adapters that give it meaning

Manifest validation must reject an unknown harness name and must know whether a harness has an
unambiguous per-user location, and `init` must detect which harnesses a project already uses. All
three needs land in this change, while the adapters that map an asset type to a destination land in
the next one.

The seam is drawn so the two cannot drift into conflict: the roster is **data only** — id, display
name, whether a per-user root exists, and the observable evidence that the harness is present — with
no destination mapping and no write behaviour. `add-harnaas-install` attaches adapters to those ids
and asserts in its registry test that every adapter's id exists in the roster. The alternative,
deferring the roster into `install`, would have forced this change to accept any string as a harness
name and then reject it two phases later, at a point where the error can no longer name the manifest
line that caused it.

### `init` writes exactly one file, and its advice is only advice

`init` writes `harnaas.json` and nothing else: no harness directory, no `.harnaas/`, no `AGENTS.md`,
no `CLAUDE.md`, no ignore-file entry. Remaining setup is printed as guidance naming the command that
performs it, and there is deliberately no flag that makes `init` perform it.

The reason is ownership. A destination is managed only when the lockfile records it
([0001](../../../docs/adr/0001-ownership-lives-in-the-lockfile.md)), and `init` writes no lockfile —
so anything else it created would be *unmanaged*, and the very next `install` would report a conflict
against `init`'s own output. Entries in the ignore file have the same problem in reverse: `install`
maintains a managed block listing exactly the paths it installed, and an entry written before anything
is installed is a claim about files that do not exist. Keeping `init` to one file is what makes both
of those rules hold without special cases.

### Interactive is an affordance, never the only path

Every workflow is completable from a non-interactive terminal, and no information is reachable only
through a prompt, picker or full-screen interface. For `init` the form is a convenience over a
flag-driven path that is always available and is selected automatically when no terminal is attached.
This is not accessibility theatre: the primary consumers of these commands are CI jobs and coding
agents, neither of which has a terminal, and a workflow that only a human can complete is a workflow
CI cannot enforce.

Prompts render through an accessible-mode wrapper rather than the form library directly, and colour
comes from the terminal's own base palette with body text left unstyled, so output stays legible on a
light background and inverts with the user's theme.

### Logging is structured, file-bound and free of user content

Diagnostics go to a log file through `log/slog`, never to the terminal, so they can never interleave
with user output or corrupt a `--json` document. The privacy rule is inherited verbatim and treated as
hard: identifiers, paths, durations, counts and outcomes may be logged; file contents, memory or prompt
text, captured output and credentials may not. For harnaas this is sharper than usual, because the
files it handles — a team's instructions and rules — are exactly the ones nobody expects to find copied
into a log they did not know existed.

### Static analysis encodes the architecture rules, and the message names the replacement

# harnaas

A CLI that manages a project's AI-harness configuration as a declared, versioned dependency. A team
states which assets it wants in a manifest; `harnaas install` fetches them and places them where each
harness expects; `harnaas lint` verifies that what is installed still matches what was declared.

## Language

### The things being managed

**Harness**:
An AI coding tool that reads its configuration from files in a project or a user home — Claude Code,
Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI.
_Avoid_: agent, editor, client, host, IDE

**Asset**:
A single unit of harness configuration that harnaas installs — one skill, rule, instruction, command
or persona.
_Avoid_: artifact, resource, plugin, extension, capability

### Asset types

**Skill**:
An asset the harness loads on its own initiative when its description matches the task at hand.
_Avoid_: capability

**Rule**:
Always-on guidance installed as its own file, which the harness discovers and loads automatically.
Untracked by version control.

**Instruction**:
Always-on guidance that harnaas concatenates into a managed block in the project's committed memory
file. Distinct from a rule in that it survives a fresh clone without anyone having run install, and
cannot be scoped to particular paths. Project scope only — at user scope there is no clone, so the
distinction from a rule disappears.

**Command**:
An asset the user invokes deliberately by typing a token for it.

**Persona**:
A delegated worker with its own model and tool budget, which the harness dispatches work to.
_Avoid_: agent, subagent

### The two files

**Manifest**:
`harnaas.json` — the committed, hand-edited declaration of which assets a project wants and where
they come from.
_Avoid_: config, declaration, settings

**Lockfile**:
`harnaas.lock.json` — the machine-written record of what was actually installed and from which
commit. Committed alongside the manifest.
_Avoid_: manifest — note that the entire.io codebase harnaas borrows its architecture from uses
"manifest" for precisely this file and "metadata" for the declaration. harnaas follows npm and Cargo
instead. Do not "correct" this.

### Installing

**Source**:
Where an asset's content comes from — a path within a GitHub repository at some ref, or a path under
the project's `.harnaas` directory.

**Scope**:
Which root an asset installs beneath — `project` for the repository's own harness directory, `user`
for the harness's per-user home.

**Managed**:
Describes a destination recorded in the lockfile. harnaas may update or remove a managed destination,
because it put it there.

cmd/harnaas/cli/manifest/assetref.go implements the asset string grammar, choosing between the keyed remote form and the project-local form by prefix rather than by trying one and falling back, so a string in neither form is reported as what it is instead of as a failed parse of a form its author never used

key_learnings: The interpretation layer does not earn its own package under harnaas's stated extraction rule. `manifest` and a hypothetical `assets` package would both be imported by the same callers (the flat cli package, and add-harnaas-install's adapters), so there is no import cycle to break — the rule says the code belongs in `manifest`. golangci-lint's `errname` rejects a type named `Violation` that has an `Error() string` method, demanding the `XxxError` form. Renaming the method to `String()` is the better fix than renaming the type: a single violation is never what a command returns, so it should not satisfy `error` at all, and the linter's complaint turned out to be pointing at a real design question.

`unparam` with check-exported fires on an unexported constructor whose field parameter always receives the same value, which will happen to every helper written ahead of the call sites that will vary it. `path.Ext` treats a leading dot as the whole extension, so stripping unconditionally turns `.editorconfig` into an empty id. Only a non-empty remainder can replace the leaf.

testifylint's useless-assert rejects `assert.Equal(t, f(), f())`, which is the obvious way to write 'this function returns a stable list'. Comparing both calls against a literal expected slice is what the linter wants and is a stronger assertion anyway, because it pins the order rather than only its stability.

The Bash tool's working directory persists between calls, so a `cd` into a package directory silently rescopes a later `go test ./...` or `golangci-lint run ./...` to that package — which reports 0 issues and looks like a pass. Prefix repo-wide verification with an explicit cd to the repository root.
